title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan presents awards to winners of 3rd Shri Arun Jaitley Memorial Debate at Shri Ram College of Commerce
subtitle:
A debate in Shri Arun Jaitley’s name is a fitting tribute to his legacy: Vice-President

Questions are essential to democracy, but should be raised to develop, not disrupt: Vice-President

AI challenges can be converted into opportunities; Rajya Sabha working towards AI-enabled translation in all Eighth Schedule languages: Vice-President

Never let algorithms become a substitute for your intellect. Human creativity can never be replaced by AI: Vice President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan today called upon young Indians to question, think critically and act with a strong sense of responsibility towards society and the nation.
Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Award Ceremony of the 3rd Shri Arun Jaitley Memorial Debate at Shri Ram College of Commerce, University of Delhi, today.

He presented awards to the winners and felicitated distinguished SRCC alumni for their exceptional achievements across various fields.

Remembering Shri Arun Jaitley Ji, the Vice-President said that a debate in his name is a fitting tribute to his legacy of leadership, intellectual engagement and exceptional oratory.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 25, 2026
Addressing the award ceremony of the 3rd Shri Arun Jaitley Memorial Debate at Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), University of Delhi, the Vice-President said questioning is an essential pillar of democracy.
“Without asking questions, there is no democracy. But questions should be asked wherever required, not to disrupt, but to develop,” he said.
Urging students to exercise independent judgement, he said: “Before supporting anyone, you should ask whether it will be beneficial for society and the nation. If you have that mindset, India will become a developed country before 2047.”
Congratulating SRCC on completing 100 years, the Vice-President, who is also Chancellor of the University of Delhi, said a century is “not just a measure of time; it is a measure of character.”
He said institutions endure when they remain rooted in their values while continuously renewing themselves, responding to changing times and preparing for the future.
Describing Shri Arun Jaitley as a distinguished SRCC alumnus, political leader, organiser and accomplished orator, the Vice-President said he represented a rare combination of legal acumen, political understanding, economic vision and exceptional communication skills.
“Democracy is not strengthened by avoiding disagreement. Democracy is strengthened when disagreement is engaged through reason, evidence, and dialogue,” he said.
Recalling his interactions with Shri Jaitley during the tenure of former Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee, the Vice-President highlighted his contribution to nation-building in several important capacities, including as Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs.
He noted Shri Jaitley’s role in major reforms including GST, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, taxation and fiscal reforms, and measures strengthening India’s financial and economic architecture. He also highlighted his contribution to financial inclusion.
He said that “what better tribute to this great person than a debate”, and appreciated SRCC for commemorating its distinguished alumnus through an intellectual forum.
The Vice-President emphasised that democratic discourse requires freedom of expression, respect for opposing viewpoints, evidence-based argument and parliamentary conduct.
He appreciated the organisers for selecting contemporary issues for debate, including the right to disconnect, universal basic income, employee representation in corporate governance and human capital for Viksit Bharat @2047.
Referring to the contemporary information environment of social media, algorithms, instant reactions and short-form content, he stressed the importance of reasoned and responsible public discourse.
He congratulated all participants and award winners, saying they had demonstrated “the value of intellectual engagement and the power of words.”
Urging students to “adapt constantly and learn continuously,” the Vice-President recalled how computers, once seen by many as a threat to jobs, eventually became a major driver of India’s growth in the IT sector.
“AI is giving us challenges, but we can make AI challenges into opportunities,” he said.
Highlighting the potential of AI to address challenges in a diverse country like India, he referred to real-time language translation as a significant example.
The Vice-President said that the Rajya Sabha is working towards introducing AI-enabled translation in all languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.
At the same time, he cautioned students: “Never let algorithms become a substitute for your intellect. Human creativity can never be replaced by AI.”
Concluding, the Vice-President said the centenary of SRCC should remind everyone that “institutions become great when every generation leaves them greater than it found them.”
The Vice-President presented awards to the winners of the 3rd Shri Arun Jaitley Memorial Debate, commending all participants for their thoughtful arguments and spirited engagement with contemporary issues. He also felicitated distinguished alumni of SRCC for their exceptional achievements and contributions across various fields, acknowledging their accomplishments as a reflection of the institution’s rich legacy of excellence and leadership.
Prof. Yogesh Singh, Vice-Chancellor, University of Delhi; Shri Ajay S. Shriram, Chairman, Governing Body, SRCC; Prof. Simrit Kaur, Principal, SRCC; and Smt. Sangeeta Jaitley, spouse of Late Shri Arun Jaitley, besides distinguished faculty members, alumni, and students were present on the occasion.

title: Vice-President calls for greater strategic cooperation among Global South nations to address emerging security and developmental challenges
subtitle:
Vice-President urges coordinated global efforts to eradicate corruption

Scientific and technological advancements should serve the collective good of humanity: Vice-President

‘Think globally, engage strategically and act in cohesion’: Vice-President to IN-STEP delegates
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today called for sustained international dialogue, mutual learning and strategic cooperation to address the rapidly evolving global security and developmental challenges.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the 4th edition of the International Strategic Engagement Programme (IN-STEP) at Uprashtrapati Bhawan today. IN-STEP is jointly organised by the Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Defence and National Security Council Secretariat at the National Defence College.

Welcoming the delegates, including 25 delegates from 22 developing countries of the Global South, the Vice President highlighted the need for collective responses to emerging challenges in technology, cyberspace, artificial intelligence, energy and maritime security, climate change and supply chains. He called upon the participants to “think globally, engage strategically and act in cohesion.”
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 25, 2026
Addressing the delegates of the fourth edition of the International Strategic Engagement Programme (IN-STEP) at Up-Rashtrapati Bhawan, the Vice-President welcomed 38 international delegates and participants from India, particularly highlighting the participation of senior professionals and leaders from friendly and like-minded countries, including those from the Global South.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that IN-STEP reflects the shared commitment articulated during India’s G20 Presidency to build a sustained platform for meaningful dialogue, mutual learning and strategic engagement. He said the interconnected nature of today’s world makes it increasingly difficult for nations to address emerging challenges in isolation.
The Vice-President observed that the strategic environment is undergoing rapid transformation, with traditional security concerns increasingly intersecting with challenges relating to technology, cyberspace, artificial intelligence, energy security, economic resilience, maritime security, climate change and supply chains.
He said IN-STEP provides an opportunity to develop a broader strategic perspective, anticipate long-term implications of global developments and formulate appropriate responses.
“Think globally, engage strategically, and act in cohesion,” Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said, outlining three principles that capture the underlying philosophy of the initiative. He stressed that shared challenges can often be addressed more effectively through cooperation, coordination and collective endeavour.
The Vice-President emphasised the importance of the Global South in shaping international conversations, noting that its diverse experiences and developmental priorities offer valuable lessons in resilience, development, security, governance and cooperation.
He said India’s engagement with the Global South is guided by mutual respect, shared interests, sovereign equality and appreciation of each nation’s developmental and strategic priorities.
The Vice-President said that corruption remains one of the major challenges confronting countries of the Global South and called for coordinated efforts to eradicate it. He urged the participants to work towards building corruption-free systems at every level, emphasising the importance of integrity and transparency in public life.
Highlighting India’s generous assistance to countries of the Global South through the Vaccine Maitri initiative during the COVID-19 pandemic, he said that technological advancements and scientific inventions should benefit all of humanity. He stressed that such knowledge and innovations should be shared for the collective good of humanity, reflecting Bharat’s ethos of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ One Earth, One Family, One Future.
He commended the National Security Council Secretariat, Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Defence for bringing together the distinguished group of participants and expressed confidence that their engagement would contribute to stronger professional relationships and enhanced strategic understanding among participating nations.
The fourth edition of the International Strategic Engagement Programme (IN-STEP) brings together 38 delegates, including 25 international delegates from 22 countries, including Sri Lanka, Seychelles, Mongolia, Nepal, Mauritius, Maldives, Oman, Guyana, Chile, Argentina, the Philippines, Thailand, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan, Qatar, Myanmar, Uzbekistan and Brazil.
IN-STEP is a two-week programme jointly organised by the Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Defence and National Security Council Secretariat, in collaboration with the National Defence College. It provides a platform for senior professionals to exchange perspectives on strategic, security and developmental issues and strengthen institutional and professional linkages.The previous editions were held in March 2024, October 2024 and October-November 2025.

title: AIIA and 132 ECO Task Force Join Hands for Ashwagandha Plantation and Research in Aravalli Landscape
subtitle: 10,000 Ashwagandha Saplings to be Scientifically Monitored at Terriers Herbal Garden, Bhatti Mines
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, and 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT have launched the Ashwagandha Plantation and Research Initiative at the Terriers Herbal Garden, Bhatti Mines, South Delhi. The initiative brings together Ayurveda, medicinal plant research, biodiversity conservation and environmental restoration.
The programme was held on September 24, 2026, under the leadership of Prof. (Vaidya) Pradeep Kumar Prajapati, Director, AIIA, and Colonel Mohan Singh, Commanding Officer, 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT.
Under the collaborative initiative, 10,000 Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera (L.) Dunal) saplings will be planted and subjected to scientific monitoring. The initiative combines AIIA’s expertise in Ayurveda, medicinal plants and scientific research with the Ecological Battalion’s experience in plantation, biodiversity conservation and environmental restoration.
The Ashwagandha plants will be regularly monitored, observed and documented to generate information on their growth and adaptation under the local climatic and environmental conditions of the Aravalli landscape. The initiative will also provide an opportunity to link traditional Ayurvedic knowledge on medicinal plants with scientific research.
Speaking on the occasion, Prof. (Vaidya) Pradeep Kumar Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said, “This initiative brings together the rich Ayurvedic knowledge of medicinal plants with scientific research and ecological restoration. Ashwagandha is an important medicinal plant of Ayurveda, and its systematic cultivation, conservation and scientific documentation can contribute to both knowledge generation and biodiversity conservation. Such collaborations reflect our commitment to taking Ayurveda beyond clinical practice and strengthening its connection with nature and sustainability.”
The programme brought together Dr. Meena Deogade, Head, Department of Dravyaguna, AIIA, faculty members Dr. Shivani Ghildiyal, Associate Professor, and Dr. Bidhan Mahajon, Assistant Professor, along with PhD Research Scholars of the Department and officers and personnel of 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT.
The planning and implementation of the plantation initiative between the two organisations was coordinated by Major Jai Singh Shekhawat of 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT and Major (Dr.) Ashish Kumar of AIIA.
The initiative at Bhatti Mines has environmental significance as the area forms part of Delhi’s Southern Ridge and the Aravalli landscape. The 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT has been engaged in plantation and restoration activities in areas affected and degraded by mining.
The Terriers Herbal Garden already houses around 200 species of medicinal and Ayurvedic significance, which have been planted and conserved. These include Parijata (Harshringar), Amla (Indian Gooseberry) and Ghritkumari (Aloe Vera). AIIA has been entrusted with providing technical support for the proper maintenance, scientific management and guidance of the herbal garden.
Ashwagandha is regarded in Ayurveda as an important medicinal plant for promoting health. The National Medicinal Plants Board, Ministry of Ayush, has also undertaken the “Ashwagandha – A Health Promoter” campaign to raise awareness about its health-related importance.
The initiative seeks to link scientific research on medicinal plants with environmental restoration at Bhatti Mines, supporting biodiversity conservation and the development of an eco-friendly ecosystem.
The initiative carries the message: “Roots in Ayurveda – Conserve Biodiversity – Restore Ecosystems.” It seeks to connect India’s traditional medicinal-plant knowledge with scientific research, biodiversity conservation and efforts to restore the green landscape of the Aravallis.

title: APEDA Facilitates Export of GI-Tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to Maldives

date:

content:
The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a 1 MT consignment of GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives on 24 September 2026. The initiative is aimed at expanding international markets for India’s GI-tagged agricultural products and strengthening the participation of Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)-led brands in agri exports.
A key feature of the export-linked value chain is improved price realisation for farmers. While the prevailing market price is ₹60 per kg, farmer realisation through the export-linked channel is ₹82 per kg, representing more than 30 per cent higher realisation. The initiative also provides FPOs an opportunity to participate more closely in export-oriented value chains and connect producers with international markets.
The consignment, exported by M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, through its FPO-led brand, will be transported to the Maldives by sea.
Gulbarga Tur Dal, associated with the Kalaburagi region of Karnataka, received Geographical Indication (GI) registration in 2019. The product is recognised for its distinctive taste and quality and forms an important part of the agricultural economy of the region. APEDA lists Gulbarga Tur Dal among Karnataka’s registered GI products.
Karnataka is one of India’s major agricultural states, with pulses playing an important role in its dryland agriculture and rural economy. Kalaburagi is one of the major centres of tur cultivation and production in the state, and Gulbarga Tur Dal represents the region’s distinctive agricultural identity.
Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev, highlighted the importance of taking India’s GI-tagged agricultural products to global markets and creating stronger market linkages for farmers. He said the export of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives provides an opportunity to build the product’s global identity while opening avenues for further market expansion.
The export is expected to pave the way for regular shipments of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives, creating sustained market opportunities for producers and exporters from Karnataka. It will also support greater value realisation for farmers and enable FPOs and farmers to integrate more closely with export-oriented value chains.
The consignment was flagged off in the presence of Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev. Senior APEDA officers and industry representatives, including Senior Consultant, APEDA Dr. Tarun Bajaj; General Manager, APEDA Smt. Vinita Sudhanshu, Managing Director KSPAML, Gulbarga Shri V. Sadashiva; and Shri Imran Pasha of M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, attended the event.

The 11th Meeting of the National Traders’ Welfare Board (NTWB) was convened at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, in hybrid mode. The Board reviewed a range of measures concerning trader welfare, Ease of Doing Business, digital empowerment, access to finance, Centre–State coordination and export promotion. The deliberations also covered issues relating to GST, MSMEs, trader grievance redressal, digital platforms and strengthening institutional support for traders, retailers, manufacturers, exporters and service providers.
During the deliberations, the members discussed GST-related matters, including rationalisation, refund delays, lengthy audits, amnesty schemes, ITC anomalies and resolution of pending appeals. Discussions on MSME and finance included inclusion of traders in MSME facilitation committees, a proposal for a centralised loan portal with 30-day timelines, reforms in the CIBIL score mechanism and establishment of traders’ grievance helplines.
Members also discussed trader welfare issues, including timely payments to government contractors, safeguards against technical penalties, relaxation in loan repayment during lean periods and enhanced Centre–State coordination. On digital empowerment, the Board deliberated on expansion of ONDC and DigiDukaan to the district level, Women Entrepreneurship Facilitation Desks under NITI Aayog, POSH cells for grievance redressal and strengthening of cyber fraud redressal mechanisms.
Special emphasis was laid on enhancing export participation by traders and MSMEs, increasing awareness regarding export opportunities, strengthening institutional support mechanisms and promoting India’s emergence as a globally competitive trading nation. The Board also discussed the need for thematic committees and focused working groups to examine sector-specific issues and provide structured recommendations for policy intervention.
The meeting was chaired by Chairman, NTWB, Shri Sunil J. Singhi. He apprised the Board of major initiatives undertaken towards achieving its objectives. Shri Singhi highlighted the Government’s commitment to trader welfare through reforms such as the Jan Vishwas Act, which rationalises 40,000 compliances, Ease of Doing Business measures and the establishment of State Traders’ Welfare Boards in Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Written confirmations from Goa and Telangana were also noted, along with progress on District Facilitation Centres.
Shri Singhi further highlighted the successful conduct of 100 consecutive virtual conferences, which have strengthened Centre–State engagement. He also referred to initiatives and campaigns including the celebration of Bhamashah Jayanti as Rashtriya Vyaapari Diwas on 29 June by Swadeshi Jagran Manch, Vyapari Samvaad in Dehradun and Indore, and Tiranga Yatra activities in Chandigarh and Indore.
The Chairman also apprised Members of developments relating to Next Generation GST 2.0 reforms, ONDC integration and expansion of DigiDukaan. DigiDukaan, a B2B procurement and Kirana digitisation initiative by ONDC, is enabling kirana stores to digitise procurement through a single ordering interface, with over 19,000 retailers currently live across Hyderabad and Jaipur.
At the outset of the meeting, Director, DPIIT, Shri Yuvraj Ravindra Patil, welcomed the Board Members and Ex-Officio Members from line Ministries and Departments and outlined the mandate of the NTWB. He emphasised the importance of promoting the Board’s initiatives and ensuring wider dissemination of DPIIT’s interactive video conference sessions.
Members were also apprised of forthcoming reforms, including the Consumer Protection (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposed to be effective from 1 January 2027, aimed at enhancing Ease of Living. The Board also deliberated on the India–UK CETA negotiations, with emphasis on export promotion.
The meeting was attended by non-official Members representing trade associations and States/UTs, along with ex officio Members from various Ministries and Departments of the Government of India.
The meeting concluded with a reaffirmation of the Board’s commitment to creating an enabling environment for traders through policy advocacy, digital empowerment, Ease of Doing Business reforms, social security initiatives and stronger Centre–State coordination. The Board reiterated its resolve to work towards the welfare and empowerment of traders and their employees and contribute actively to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: TRAI Launches Digital Connectivity Rating Platform
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today launched the Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Platform, an integrated digital platform designed to provide visibility of rating of properties to the consumers and facilitate the end-to-end process for rating the digital connectivity of properties along with a mobile app for testing digital connectivity.
The DCR Platform facilitates implementation of the framework prescribed under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Rating of Properties for Digital Connectivity) Regulations, 2024, as amended by the Rating of Properties for Digital Connectivity (Amendment) Regulation, 2026, notified on 13 May 2026 and rating process specified in Rating Manual 2026, issued by TRAI on 9 June 2026.
The platform provides a public interface for consumers to view the properties rated for digital connectivity. It brings Property Managers (PMs) registered Digital Connectivity Rating Agency (DCRA) and consumer onto a common digital interface. Property Managers can register their properties in category of Public, Government, Commercial, Private etc., submit rating applications, upload the prescribed information and documents, select a registered DCRA and track the status of their application through the platform. The platform supports the prescribed assessment workflow for both constructed and under-construction properties.   Registered DCRAs can access assigned applications, undertake assessments, record observations and test results, manage supporting documentation and complete the rating process in accordance with the prescribed framework. The platform enables the digital workflow relating to assessment, report generation, certification and publication of ratings. Consumers and other stakeholders will be able to search rated properties, view published ratings, verify the corresponding certificates and compare the properties of interest.
Field assessments will be facilitated through a dedicated DCRA mobile app. The app will enable authorised DCRA to undertake in-building digital connectivity measurements in accordance with the prescribed testing methodology. Property information received through the web portal and the assessment data captured through the mobile application will be synchronised in the platform. The platform integrates eSign for the digital signing and verification of documents and certificates. It also supports online payment of applicable rating fees, email and SMS alerts, and secure storage of property records, test results, certificates and audit logs.
For Consumers, the platform offers a public rating search page. Consumers can search for a rated property by property name, certificate ID or location. They can view the property’s digitally signed rating certificate and verify its authenticity through the QR code provided on the certificate. This will make digital connectivity a visible and verifiable attribute of a rated property and empowers consumers with connectivity information. Based on this information consumer can make an informed choice while selecting the desired property prior to making the final purchase or lease decision.
Speaking on the occasion,
Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman
, TRAI, said, “The Digital Connectivity Rating Platform establishes a transparent and standardised framework for assessing the digital connectivity readiness of properties. By making ratings publicly searchable and verify the certificates, the platform will empower consumers with credible and comparable information. It will help them make more informed choices about homes and offices with strong and reliable connectivity, supporting smoother calls, downloads and access to online services. It will also enable consumers to recognise the value of digital connectivity infrastructure built into a property, while encouraging Property Managers to plan such infrastructure at the appropriate stage of property development.
”
About the Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Framework
The DCR framework provides a standardised method for evaluating digital connectivity within properties. The assessment considers prescribed parameters relating to fibre readiness, mobile network availability, in-building solutions and Wi-Fi infrastructure, with applicable benchmarks for different categories of properties. The framework seeks to encourage the consideration of Digital Connectivity Infrastructure at appropriate stages of property development and facilitate the assessment of infrastructure and connectivity performance in existing properties. The Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Platform can be accessed at:
https://dcrp.trai.gov.in
For additional queries, please contact: Ms. Archna Ahlawat, Advisor (IT) at
advisorit@trai.gov.in

date:

content:
Odisha’s diverse cultural heritage takes center stage in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, with a collection of artefacts showcasing the state’s traditions of devotion, craftsmanship, painting, textiles and literature. The catalogue features a wide range of works centered on Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Devi Subhadra, alongside representations of Odisha’s regional deities, traditional art forms, textiles, festivals and prominent cultural figures.
Among the notable pieces is a Jagannath Parivar on Chariot, depicting Lord Jagannath, Devi Subhadra and Lord Balabhadra seated on an intricately detailed chariot drawn by four sculpted horses, a representation of the cultural and spiritual significance of Rath Yatra.
The collection also includes a Pattachitra painting depicting the Puri Rath Yatra, portraying the deities in their chariot amid scenes of dance, music and celebration, highlighting the work's intricate detailing, vibrant colours and connection with Odisha's devotional artistic traditions.
The auction catalogue also showcases several traditional crafts associated with the state. Among them are works in Cuttack silver filigree or Tarakasi, an intricate craft involving delicate silver wires, as well as Sambalpuri textiles and Ikat.
Another featured work is a Maa Samaleswari devotional icon created using Sambalpuri Ikat, with the artwork entirely hand-woven through the traditional Bandha technique.
Beyond Jagannath-themed works, the collection captures Odisha's vibrant festival traditions. A framed print documents the Panchu Dola Melana, showing devotees carrying colourful miniature temple structures, while another photograph captures the festival at Chilika Lake, featuring boats carrying village deities for their annual gathering.
Taken together, the 62 mementos present a broad visual narrative of Odisha, from the enduring traditions of Jagannath worship and Rath Yatra to Pattachitra, Tarakasi, Sambalpuri Ikat, regional festivals and literary heritage. Rather than representing a single artistic tradition, the catalogue brings together multiple expressions of the state's living cultural heritage in one collection.

MEE-TR 2026 to introduce ‘Solid Waste Management’ as a separate Evaluation Criterion of Tiger Reserves
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 2:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today launched the Inception Workshop for the 6th Cycle of Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves in India (MEE-TR), organised by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), in New Delhi.
The inception workshop marked the commencement of the 6th Cycle of MEE-TR, which will cover all 58 Tiger Reserves in the country. The workshop brought together representatives of NTCA, WII, State Forest Departments, Tiger Reserve management teams and experts to discuss the framework, methodology and implementation of the 6th Cycle.
In his inaugural address, Shri Bhupender Yadav highlighted that India has demarcated over 85,000 sq km for tiger conservation. He emphasized the need to continuously integrate evolving scientific processes and technologies into wildlife conservation and evaluation. At the same time, he stressed that a science-based approach must be guided by compassion, values and vision to ensure harmonious engagement between forest departments and local communities. He acknowledged the contribution of generations of forest officials in fostering a sense of belongingness towards wildlife conservation in the society.
The Minister suggested that local ecological and sociological experts should contribute to the evaluation of MEE reports, besides local youth being involved in the MEE exercise. He emphasized that evaluation outcomes should reflect the specific needs and challenges of individual Tiger Reserves, with ecosystem preservation and sociological balance informing policy interventions.
Shri Yadav called for area-based assessment of human-wildlife conflict and measurable conservation outcomes. He further emphasized the need for site-specific landscape management and adaptive conservation practices that incorporate local socio-economic considerations. He stressed that professionalism and objectivity should remain central to the MEE exercise, ensuring that assessments provide a robust basis for strengthening conservation management.
Addressing the session, Union MoS (EFCC) Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh appreciated the dedication of senior forest officers bringing decades of administrative and conservation experience to the on-ground MEE exercise. He noted that their extensive knowledge and field experience constitute a valuable repository of institutional learning for future generations of wildlife conservationists.
MEE-TR is a systematic and evidence-based assessment of how effectively a Tiger Reserve is being managed to achieve its conservation objectives. It examines management actions as well as the adequacy of planning, resources and management systems and whether these efforts are translating into desired conservation results. In India, MEE is undertaken using a framework adapted from the IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA) Framework for Assessing Management Effectiveness. The framework assesses six elements: Context, Planning, Inputs, Processes, Outputs and Outcomes.
MEE was initiated in India in 2006. Five assessment cycles have been completed in 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022, covering 28, 39, 43, 50 and 51 Tiger Reserves respectively. The 6th Cycle builds on the experience of previous assessments while strengthening the focus on field-based evidence, management outcomes, emerging threats, digital and spatial information and continuous improvement. A significant new feature of MEE-TR 2026 is the introduction of ‘Solid Waste Management’ as a separate evaluation criterion. The criterion will focus on sustainable waste management practices within Tiger Reserves, with particular attention to waste generated at forest chowkis, waste arising from tourism activities and biomedical waste generated at wildlife rescue centres.
The assessment will cover major components of Tiger Reserve management, including tiger and prey conservation, habitat management, protection and wildlife crime, wildlife monitoring and health, fire and disaster management, human-wildlife coexistence, community engagement, tourism management, landscape connectivity and management planning and resources. The assessment will be undertaken by independent multidisciplinary evaluation teams, and will seek to identify management strengths, gaps and areas requiring improvement, while providing a basis for prioritising management actions and resources.
The technical sessions of the workshop covered perspectives and insights on MEE-TR, its genesis and evolution, criteria and indicators of the MEE-Tiger Reserves framework and operational modalities and logistics for field visits. The Technical Manual of MEE 2026 was also released during the inaugural session, providing the framework for the sixth-cycle evaluation.

title: Union Environment Minister launches Workshop on ‘Capacity Enhancement for Effective Forest Management Project’, in collaboration with JICA, in New Delhi
subtitle: Project must focus on Region-specific Capacity-building Modules reflecting Local Knowledge and Challenges; Need Tangible Action based on latest Scientific Approaches and Emerging Technologies: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:

                25 SEP 2026 10:57AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (EFCC) Shri Bhupender Yadav today launched the Workshop on
‘Capacity Enhancement for Effective Forest Management Project’
, organised by the Ministry in collaboration with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), in New Delhi. The workshop was attended by senior officers of the Ministry and Senior Representative, JICA India. Representatives from Forest Departments of various States/UTs, Indian Research Institutions and Central Training Institutes in the field of forestry also participated.
The Capacity Enhancement project (2025-26 to 2031-32) seeks to enhance the capacity of frontline forest personnel in view of changing forest and wildlife management requirements, emerging climate and environmental concerns, and their increasingly diverse responsibilities in the field. It also envisages strengthening research and development to translate knowledge and research outcomes into improved training and sustainable forest management practices.
Addressing the inaugural session of the workshop, Shri Yadav highlighted that the project marks an important milestone in the decades-long cooperation between India and Japan in the forestry sector. He emphasised that forests are critical for addressing climate change, conserving biodiversity and supporting the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities. The Minister underlined the need for strengthening the capacity of frontline forest personnel from both operational and administrative perspectives.
Highlighting forest fire management as a global challenge, Shri Yadav said the project holds significant potential for enhancing technical and field-level capabilities in forest fire management, biodiversity conservation and climate action. He stressed that capacity building should go beyond classroom training and focus on the application of modern technologies and field-level best practices, while integrating the knowledge and experience of local communities.
The Minister further emphasised the importance of developing region-specific capacity-building modules that reflect local knowledge and challenges. He outlined key components of the project, including research and development for practical technological solutions, pilot projects for field-level application, strengthening training institutions for practice-oriented training, and sharing of best practices with SAARC and other developing countries. He called for translating the workshop’s deliberations into tangible action on the ground by combining traditional knowledge, scientific approaches and emerging technologies.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Eiji Wakamatsu, Senior Representative, JICA India Office, said the project aims to become a platform bringing together Indian and Japanese research institutions to develop solutions to global challenges and strengthen India’s leadership in the Global South in the fields of forest management, climate change and capacity building. He noted that JICA’s partnership with India in the forestry sector spans nearly three decades and has benefited more than 7 lakh people.
Mr. Wakamatsu highlighted that the second phase of the project, covering 2025-26 to 2031-32, focuses on wood transformation and livelihood generation, digital transformation for improved forest management, and collaborative academic research. He expressed JICA’s commitment to further deepening collaboration with the Union and State Governments in India for sustainable forest management and capacity enhancement.
It was informed earlier by ADG (Wildlife), MoEFCC, Shri Ramesh Pandey that the project has a total outlay of Rs. 537.10 crore, including a JICA contribution of Rs. 440.42 crore and Government of India share of Rs. 96.68 crore. The project is being implemented over seven years, from 2025-26 to 2031-32. The project will involve all States in India, with priority given to new participating States, while also supporting States that were previously included in a related project.
The project builds upon the earlier JICA-supported initiative and seeks to further strengthen sustainable forest management and the capabilities of frontline forest staff. The occasion also witnessed the release of the Project Brochure, outlining the key objectives and areas of cooperation under the project. The technical session of the workshop witnessed a presentation by the Ministry on the objectives and scope of the project, perspectives from JICA representatives and an interactive session with States, Research Institutions and Central Training Institutes.

content:
The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has successfully concluded a three-city Investor Outreach Programme for the upcoming e-auction of 459 land parcels of Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.
As part of the programme, Investor Meets were organised in Visakhapatnam on September 23, Vijayawada on September 24 and Hyderabad on September 25, 2026. The programme was undertaken to provide prospective buyers, investors, developers and other stakeholders with detailed information about the land portfolio and the e-auction process ahead of the scheduled auction in October.
The Investor Meet in Visakhapatnam witnessed participation from more than 150 prospective buyers and other stakeholders in person, while more than 50 additional participants joined the programme through video conferencing. A number of participants joining virtually were NRIs and prospective buyers based outside India. Their queries regarding the properties, eligibility, auction process and other aspects of the transaction were also addressed by the officials during the interaction.
The subsequent Investor Meets in Vijayawada and Hyderabad saw participation of approximately 50–60 people each, including prospective buyers and stakeholders seeking information about the properties and the auction process.
The interactions across the three cities covered the location and characteristics of the land parcels, plot sizes, applicable terms and conditions, eligibility requirements, registration procedure, Earnest Money Deposit (EMD), bidding process and other aspects relevant to participation in the e-auction.
During the Investor Meets, Executive Director, NLMC, Shri Pradeep Kumar; General Manager, NLMC, Shri Sunil Sahu; and General Manager (HR), RINL, Shri Binay Prasad, addressed queries from prospective buyers and other interested stakeholders regarding the properties, auction process and related procedures. Questions raised by participants joining through video conferencing, including NRIs and prospective buyers based outside India, were also addressed during the Visakhapatnam interaction.
459 Land Parcels Across Established Locations of Visakhapatnam
The RINL land portfolio being offered through e-auction comprises 459 land parcels aggregating 93,572.21 square yards, located at HB Colony, Maddilapalem and Auto Nagar, Gajuwaka, Visakhapatnam. The individual plot sizes range from approximately 128.94 square yards to 2,728 square yards.
The portfolio comprises 456 residential plots at HB Colony, covering approximately 87,949.77 square yards, and three plots at Auto Nagar, Gajuwaka, aggregating approximately 5,622.44 square yards.
The HB Colony portfolio is located in an established residential area of Visakhapatnam, with access to existing road and civic infrastructure. The Auto Nagar parcels are situated in an established commercial and industrial area.
At Auto Nagar, the portfolio includes a 2,728-square-yard contiguous parcel in Block 2, as well as two residential plots in Block 3 aggregating approximately 2,894.44 square yards.
Quikr India Pvt. Ltd. (QIPL) has been appointed as the Transaction Consultant for the e-auction process.
E-Auction to be Conducted in Two Sessions
The e-auction will be conducted through the RailTel E-Nivida e-Procurement Platform in two sessions. Day 1 will be held on October 12, 2026, comprising 243 plots, with the auction scheduled from 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM. The last date for registration and submission of EMD for Day 1 is October 8, 2026, up to 5:00 PM.
Day 2 will be held on October 16, 2026, comprising 216 plots, with the auction scheduled from 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM. The last date for registration and submission of EMD for Day 2 is October 14, 2026, up to 5:00 PM. The Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) is ₹2 lakh per auction.
Prospective bidders can access the auction details, registration process, plot information and applicable terms and conditions through the official e-auction portal: https://eauction.enivida.com
Shri Rohan Chand Thakur, CEO, NLMC, said,
“The successful completion of the three-city Investor Outreach Programme is an important milestone ahead of the RINL land e-auction. The meetings in Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Hyderabad enabled us to engage directly with prospective buyers and provide them with detailed information on the land portfolio, the transaction process and the applicable terms and conditions. The participation across the three cities, including virtual participation from NRIs and prospective buyers based outside India, provided an opportunity to address queries from a wider pool of interested participants. NLMC remains committed to facilitating a transparent and structured mechanism for the monetisation of non-core assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises.”
Following the completion of the three-city Investor Outreach Programme, QIPL, the Transaction Consultant, along with the RINL team, will remain stationed at the project venue on a daily basis until the auction to assist prospective buyers and address queries relating to the land parcels and the e-auction process.
The teams will facilitate access to relevant project information and provide clarifications to interested participants regarding the properties, auction procedure, registration requirements, EMD and other applicable terms and conditions.
The October e-auction represents the next stage in the structured process for monetisation of RINL’s identified non-core land assets. The outreach programme has provided prospective buyers and stakeholders across the region, as well as participants joining virtually from outside India, an opportunity to familiarise themselves with the portfolio and the auction mechanism well in advance of the bidding dates.
About NLMC
National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a 100% Government of India-owned company under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. Established to facilitate the monetisation of surplus land and non-core assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and other Government entities, NLMC works with CPSEs and concerned stakeholders to identify, structure and facilitate the monetisation of such assets.
NLMC supports the process through structured asset assessment, transaction facilitation, market outreach and coordination with relevant stakeholders, with the objective of enabling a transparent and systematic approach to public asset monetisation.
About RINL
Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, is a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, Government of India. RINL operates the integrated steel plant at Visakhapatnam and has played a significant role in the development of the steel sector and the industrial ecosystem of the region.
The company has a substantial land and asset base associated with its operations. In coordination with NLMC, RINL is facilitating the structured monetisation of identified non-core land assets through a transparent and competitive e-auction process.

content:
The Government of India, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), has decided to borrow ₹7,86,000 crore in the second half (H2) of FY 2026-27. This includes Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs) issuance of ₹15,000 crore
During FY 2026-27, Government of India is expected to have
Market Borrowing of ₹15,99,506 crore through dated securities, as compared to Budget Estimates of ₹17,20,000 crore for FY 2026-27.
The gross market borrowing of ₹7,86,000 crore in H2: 2026-27 shall be completed through 23 weekly auctions.
The market borrowing will be spread over securities of tenor 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 30, 40 and 50 years. The share of borrowing
(including SGrBs)

The Government will continue to carry out switching/buyback of securities to smoothen the redemption profile.
The Government will continue to reserve the right to exercise greenshoe option to retain an additional subscription of up to ₹2,000 crore against each of the securities indicated in the auction notifications.
During the third Quarter of FY 2026-27, Government is expected to borrow ₹23,000 crore per week in 13 auction weeks through issuance of Treasury Bills (T-Bills). The break up would be ₹8,000 crore under 91-day T Bills, ₹8,000 crore under 182-day T-Bills and ₹7,000 crore under 364-day T-Bills.
To take care of temporary mismatches in Government accounts, if any, RBI has fixed the Ways and Means Advances (WMA) limit for H2 of FY 2026-27 at ₹50,000 crore.

title: DRI seizes 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold worth around Rs. 15 crore at Mumbai airport; three arrested
subtitle: Gold powder ingeniously blended with food products like milk powder, oats, rice flour and cake mix
date:

                25 SEP 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Continuing its sustained crackdown on gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Mumbai Zonal Unit, based on specific intelligence, intercepted three Indian passengers arriving from Dubai at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai, in the early hours of 23.09.2026, with operational assistance from the Air Intelligence Unit (AIU), Mumbai Airport Customs.
Detailed examination of their baggage revealed a highly sophisticated and unusual method of concealment, wherein foreign-origin gold had been converted into fine powder and meticulously mixed with packaged food products of similar colour, texture and consistency to evade detection.
The gold powder was found concealed across several apparently ordinary food packets like milk powder, oats, various flours, Nutella and coconut milk powder. In all, approximately 33.50 kg food products mixed with gold powder were recovered from the baggage of the three passengers.
Through careful segregation and assaying, 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold, valued at approximately Rs. 14.81 crore, was recovered and seized under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962. During questioning, all three passengers admitted to acting on behalf of the same organised gold-smuggling syndicate. They were accordingly arrested under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
The operation has uncovered a novel and sophisticated method of gold smuggling, wherein powdered gold was ingeniously blended with a wide variety of packaged food products to evade routine detection.

title: DRI seizes over 125,000 kg foreign-origin smuggled areca nuts and 41,000 kg poppy seeds worth around Rs. 20.31 crore in Assam and Mizoram in a crackdown on cross-border smuggling; four arrested
subtitle: This is one of the largest seizure of smuggled areca nuts in North-East Region
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Continuing its sustained crackdown on cross-border smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has seized 1,25,680 kg of foreign-origin areca nuts and 41,697 kg foreign-origin poppy seeds, collectively valued at approximately Rs. 20.31 crore, in two intelligence-led operations in Mizoram and Assam. Four persons have been arrested in connection with the transportation of the smuggled poppy seeds.
On 23-24.09.26, in a major intelligence led operation in Mizoram, DRI with the assistance of Customs Champhai, 14th Battalion Assam Rifles and Champhai Police, searched three godowns in and around Ruantlang village, Champhai District, located approximately 20 km from the Indo-Myanmar border. All the premises were found locked and unattended. The search of the premises resulted in the recovery of 1,25,680 kg suspected foreign-origin areca nuts valued at around Rs. 14 Crore and 25,440 kg of poppy seeds valued at Rs. 3.81 crore. Preliminary investigation indicated that the goods had been smuggled into India from Myanmar. The goods were seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
Earlier on 22.09.26, based on specific intelligence regarding transportation of foreign-origin poppy seeds from the Mizoram border area towards Assam, DRI officers with the assistance of 38 Battalion Assam Rifles, intercepted two trucks near Lailapur, Silchar. Detailed examination and rummaging of the vehicles resulted in the recovery of 290 HDPE bags containing 16,257 kg foreign-origin poppy seeds. The bags bore markings indicative of foreign manufacture and trade, and the consignment was not accompanied by valid import documents. The poppy seeds, valued at approximately Rs 2.43 crore, along with the two vehicles, were seized under the Customs Act, 1962. Four persons involved in the transportation were arrested.
The seizure of foreign-origin smuggled areca nuts, one of the largest seizures of the commodity in recent years in the North-Eastern region of the country, is a significant achievement in DRI’s efforts to curb cross-border smuggling.
Poppy seeds are classified as a “Restricted” item under the ITC (HS) Classification of the Foreign Trade Policy, with import permitted subject to specified conditions, including sourcing from designated countries and registration of import contracts with the Narcotics Commissioner, Gwalior.
The seizures highlight DRI’s continued focus on intercepting smuggling networks operating through the vulnerable India-Myanmar border and preventing illicit entry of restricted and foreign-origin agricultural commodities into the country.

title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Arogya Manthan 2026, marking eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of ABDM
subtitle:
AB PM-JAY and ABDM Milestones Reflect India’s Expanding Digital and Health Assurance Ecosystem: Shri J.P. Nadda

AB PM-JAY Emerges as World’s Largest Health Assurance Programme, Covering Over 60 Crore Beneficiaries: Union Health Minister

Arogya Manthan 2026 launches a series of digital health and health assurance initiatives, including National Healthcare Providers Registry Mobile App, Secure Data Environment and Auto-Adjudication Framework for AB PM-JAY

Arogya Manthan 2026 recognises States and Union Territories for excellence in implementation of AB PM-JAY and ABDM across various categories
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J.P. Nadda, today inaugurated Aarogya Manthan 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, marking eight years of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) and five y ears of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). Organised by the National Health Authority (NHA), the event brought together senior government officials, healthcare providers, insurers, technology and digital health experts, academia, development partners and other stakeholders to deliberate on the progress of India’s health assurance and digital health ecosystem and the priorities for its next phase.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J.P. Nadda, congratulated all stakeholders on the completion of eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of ABDM. He said that these milestones provide an opportunity to take stock of the progress made and renew the commitment towards the welfare of the poor and marginalised sections of society, in line with the hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of  “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas.”
Shri Nadda highlighted the significant expansion of AB PM-JAY since its inception and said that the scheme has emerged as the world’s largest health assurance programme, with more than 60 crore beneficiaries covered and over 13 crore hospital admissions facilitated, involving treatment worth more than Rs. 2 lakh crores.
He noted that the Government further expanded the scheme to cover all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status, bringing them within its ambit. He also highlighted the importance of portability under the scheme, particularly for migrant workers, and appreciated the contribution of State Governments, healthcare institutions and other stakeholders in taking the programme forward.
The Union Minister said that the journey of AB PM-JAY and ABDM has demonstrated the transformative role of technology in healthcare, with digital systems supporting authentication, authorisation and access to treatment across locations. Highlighting the progress under ABDM, he said that more than 97.8 crore ABHAs have been created, with over 121 crore health records linked, while more than 5.6 lakh health facilities and around 11 lakh healthcare professionals are registered on the ABDM ecosystem. He also highlighted the development of the National Health Claims Exchange, which seeks to bring hospitals and insurers onto a common digital platform.
Referring to the initiatives launched at Aarogya Manthan 2026, Shri Nadda said that these would further strengthen digital healthcare, facilitate the secure use of health data and create new opportunities for health research, innovation and data-driven decision-making. He appreciated the National Health Authority and acknowledged the
role of
State Governments, healthcare professionals, empanelled hospitals, Ayushman Mitras, ASHA and Anganwadi workers, technology partners and other stakeholders.
Shri Nadda emphasised that the journey must continue and called for sustained efforts to leverage digital technology to make healthcare more accessible, efficient and patient-centric. He expressed confidence that the deliberations at Aarogya Manthan 2026 would generate actionable outcomes and contribute further towards strengthening India’s health ecosystem and serving humanity.
Dr. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), Niti Ayoga, congratulated the National Health Authority (NHA) on the occasion. Highlighting the transformation brought about by AB PM-JAY, he said that the scheme has enabled people, particularly from economically weaker sections, to access healthcare with greater confidence and reduced financial burden. He emphasised that the next phase should focus on strengthening continuity of care, quality and patient-centric healthcare, including seamless referral mechanisms for patients requiring specialised treatment.
Dr. Srinivas highlighted the importance of achieving wider adoption and saturation of ABHA and strengthening interoperability of digital health records, with citizen consent and appropriate safeguards. He stressed that high-quality, standardised and interoperable health data would be critical for advancing health research and responsibly leveraging Artificial Intelligence in healthcare. He also called for strengthening the National Health Claims Exchange, improving ease of claims and pre-authorisation processes, and expanding awareness of health assurance and digital health initiatives.
Shri Ajay Seth, Chairman, IRDAI, highlighted the success of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and said that the experience gained through the scheme provides an opportunity to further strengthen the health insurance ecosystem in the country. He emphasised the need to ensure quality, affordability and access in healthcare while creating value for all stakeholders, including citizens, hospitals, insurers and technology providers.
Highlighting the importance of standardisation and transparency in health insurance, Shri Seth underlined the need for wider adoption of key digital and operational building blocks, including ABHA as an identity for health insurance, codification of treatments, standard billing formats, and standard treatment protocols and guidelines. He also highlighted the role of India’s digital public infrastructure and the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX) in enabling greater interoperability and creating a more connected health insurance ecosystem. He said, “It is within our reach to provide effective healthcare for the widest possible population — affordable and with good quality.”
Speaking at the Occasion, Dr. Rajiv Bahl, DG ICMR & Secretary DHR, highlighted the significance of the eight-year milestone of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and five years of ABDM, noting that Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY has emerged as the world’s largest health assurance scheme, covering and benefiting more than 60 crore citizens. He said the focus going forward would be on further improving the quality of healthcare and expanding coverage to ensure greater benefits for citizens.
Highlighting the collaboration between DHR, ICMR and NHA, Dr Bahl outlined two key areas of work. On standardisation of treatment, he noted that treatment based on standardised algorithms can help ensure greater consistency and quality of care, with ICMR having developed more than 150 standard treatment workflows and guidelines. He also highlighted the importance of cost-effectiveness in healthcare, noting that the Health Technology Assessment in India (HTAIn) under DHR evaluates the cost-effectiveness of healthcare technologies and interventions.
Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, NHA, congratulated all stakeholders on achieving two significant milestones — eight years of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and five years of Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). He highlighted the scale and reach of both programmes, with over 49 crore Ayushman Cards and around 98 crore ABHA IDs generated across the country.
Looking ahead, he noted that Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY has generated more than 13 crore patient records, creating a valuable repository for research, development and health analytics. He said the Secure Data Environment will enable responsible use of such data while safeguarding patient identities. He also highlighted the launch of the Auto-Adjudication Framework, aimed at streamlining and strengthening the claims adjudication process under AB PM-JAY through technology and data-driven processes.
A major highlight of Arogya Manthan 2026 was the launch of a series of initiatives aimed at strengthening the digital foundations of India’s health assurance ecosystem. These included the National Healthcare Providers Registry (NHPR) Mobile App, NHCX Implementation Guide for Payers, Guidebook for a Model Digital Health Facility, Secure Data Environment (SDE) application and Framework for Auto-Adjudication of Claims under AB PM-JAY.
The Secure Data Environment, developed by the National Health Authority (NHA) with the support of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, is envisaged as a governed environment for access to and analysis of AB PM-JAY and ABDM health data. Approved entities will be able to work with de-identified data or execute code within an isolated NHA environment, with outputs reviewed before release. The initiative is intended to facilitate health research, programme planning, outcome analysis and responsible AI innovation, while incorporating safeguards for protection of personal data.
The deliberations at Arogya Manthan 2026 focused on strengthening the efficiency, quality and interoperability of health services. The session on “NHCX for Streamlining Health Insurance” examined the role of the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX) in enabling streamlined, standardised and technology-driven health insurance processes, including how interoperable digital claims infrastructure can improve efficiency, strengthen coordination across the health insurance ecosystem, and open new avenues of health financing.
This was followed by parallel sessions under the AB PM-JAY and ABDM tracks, examining key aspects of programme implementation, healthcare delivery and digital transformation.
Under the AB PM-JAY track, the session on “Claim Processing to Intelligent Assurance: Transforming AB PM-JAY” examined the use of technology, data and analytics for strengthening claims processing and programme integrity. The session on “Strategic Purchasing from the Perspective of Quality and Cost-Effectiveness” discussed approaches to improving quality of care while promoting efficient utilisation of resources.
The ABDM track included discussions on “UHI for Improving Access of Healthcare Services”, focusing on the role of digital platforms in expanding access and participation across the healthcare ecosystem, and “Leveraging Standards for Better Health Delivery”, which examined the importance of common health-data standards for seamless exchange of information and improved continuity and quality of healthcare delivery.
The event also recognised States and Union Territories for their performance under AB PM-JAY and ABDM across different categories. Under AB PM-JAY, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim and Jammu & Kashmir were recognised for the highest card saturation among ASHA, Anganwadi Worker (AWW) and Anganwadi Helper (AWH) beneficiaries in the large State, small State and Union Territory categories, respectively. Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Gujarat were recognised as the top-performing States in claim settlement for inter-State portability.
Under ABDM, Bihar, Ladakh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli were recognised as top-performing States/UTs across model districts based on district population categories. Chandigarh, Assam and Uttar Pradesh were recognised for the highest number of sub-centres using ABDM-enabled Health Management Information Systems (HMIS) in the small State/UT, medium State/UT and large State categories, respectively.

title: Union MoS for Health & Family Welfare Smt. Anupriya Patel addresses 71st Foundation Day celebrations of AIIMS New Delhi
subtitle:
Medical colleges rise from 387 to over 800 and undergraduate medical seats from 51,000 to nearly 1.3 lakh: Smt. Anupriya Patel

Smt. Patel calls upon AIIMS New Delhi to lead advanced clinical care, nurture healthcare professionals and guide the expanding AIIMS network

AIIMS New Delhi has a special responsibility as the apex mentor for medical institutions across the country: Smt. Anupriya Patel

 Smt. Patel emphasizes that technology must complement, not replace, human clinical judgement and care; stresses the health and well-being of healthcare professionals

Smt. Anupriya Patel inaugurates ‘AIIMS: Seven Decades of Healthcare Innovation’ exhibition showcasing seven decades of milestones and achievements

Over 1,500 school students to participate in health education and community outreach activities at the AIIMS exhibition
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 SEP 2026 3:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel addressed the 71st Foundation Day celebrations of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, as the Chief Guest today. The celebrations marked over seven decades of AIIMS’ contributions to healthcare, medical education, research and innovation.
Addressing the gathering, Smt. Anupriya Patel said that “since its inception in 1956, AIIMS New Delhi has occupied a special place in the healthcare journey of the country.” She highlighted its contribution to redefining medical education, pioneering groundbreaking research and delivering high-quality patient care. She underlined that “over the decades, the name AIIMS has become synonymous with clinical excellence and public trust.” She noted that while the institution has a distinguished legacy, this legacy also brings greater responsibility for the future and requires continued focus on national healthcare priorities.
Smt. Patel highlighted the transformation of India’s healthcare and medical education landscape. She noted that the country has expanded from one AIIMS at the turn of the century to a network of 23 AIIMS institutions. Since 2014, the number of medical colleges has increased from 387 to over 800, while undergraduate medical seats have increased from 51,000 to nearly 1.3 lakh, along with a substantial expansion in postgraduate opportunities.” She further added that the Government envisions adding another 75,000 medical seats to further strengthen this framework. This expansion is not merely a matter of numbers but is closely linked to equity and access.”
Smt. Patel further emphasized that “quality medical education must reach every region, advanced tertiary healthcare must be brought closer to citizens, and the country must build a strong pool of doctors, nurses, scientists and allied healthcare professionals capable of responding to changing demographic and epidemiological needs.” She added that “AIIMS New Delhi has a special responsibility in this transformation as the apex mentor and as an institution that has established a benchmark for the rest of the country.”
Speaking about the scale of healthcare services at AIIMS New Delhi, Smt. Patel said that the institution’s enormous clinical volume should not be viewed merely through statistics. Millions of outpatient visits represent individuals and families placing their trust in the institution, while admissions and surgeries represent situations in which patients entrust their lives to its doctors, nurses and support staff. She emphasised that AIIMS is therefore not only a centre of medical excellence but also an institution of public trust, and that this trust has to be earned and nurtured every day.
Smt. Patel also highlighted AIIMS’ role at the forefront of advanced medical care and emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), robotic surgery, organ transplantation and advanced diagnostics. She emphasised that “technology must remain an instrument for better patient care and should complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgement.” She noted that “AI cannot replace a physician’s intuition, a robotic arm cannot replace a surgeon’s judgement, and technology cannot replace the reassuring human presence of a nurse.” She stressed the importance of maintaining a balance between scientific advancement and the human touch in healthcare.
She also underlined that quality healthcare must also be reflected in the patient’s overall experience. She called for the AIIMS premises to be made more navigable for citizens and emphasised the importance of empathy, clear communication, dignity and patient-centred care. She also referred to the importance of patient safety and the collective responsibility of doctors, nurses, technicians and administrative personnel in ensuring safe and quality healthcare.
Smt. Patel emphasised that expansion of healthcare infrastructure must go hand in hand with quality. She noted that a new ward requires adequate nursing support, specialised services require trained professionals and digital initiatives should help reduce friction for patients. She stressed that growth and quality must progress together and that AIIMS New Delhi should continue to demonstrate that expansion in scale can coexist with high standards of patient care.
Highlighting the growing importance of preventive healthcare, Smt. Patel said that India’s health priorities increasingly focus on prevention, early detection and timely management, particularly in the context of non-communicable and lifestyle-related diseases. Referring to the shift in the policy approach towards prevention and health promotion, she called upon AIIMS to leverage its intellectual capital to contribute to public health policy, community health, lifestyle management and preventive medicine.
Smt. Patel also underlined the importance of the National Health Policy, 2017, and the broader shift towards preventive and promotive healthcare. She said that healthcare must address the country’s changing epidemiological burden while ensuring that citizens have access to affordable and quality services.
Highlighting the role of Ayushman Bharat and Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) in expanding access to healthcare and protecting vulnerable families from the financial burden of medical treatment, she noted that AB PM-JAY has completed eight years and has covered more than 62 crore beneficiaries, strengthening financial protection for people from poor and vulnerable backgrounds.
Smt. Patel further emphasized that AIIMS New Delhi must increasingly function as a national hub for capacity building and indigenous innovation. She emphasised that the impact of AIIMS should be measured not only by the number of patients treated on its campus but also by the national capacity it creates by training healthcare professionals and enabling AIIMS-level expertise to reach other parts of the country. She also stressed that research should bridge the gap between the laboratory and the patient and translate into clinical use and public benefit.
Smt. Patel also underlined the need for greater development, validation and implementation of indigenous medical technologies. She said that India cannot rely indefinitely on imported medical technologies and that academia, hospitals and Indian industry must work together to develop solutions suited to the country’s healthcare requirements. She called upon AIIMS “to contribute to an ecosystem in which India not only adopts advanced healthcare solutions but also develops them.”
Smt. Patel called for greater attention to the health and well-being of healthcare professionals themselves. She emphasised that along with treating patients, the health of doctors and other healthcare professionals is equally important for building a healthy nation. She stressed the importance of inculcating healthy habits among healthcare professionals from a young age and promoting a culture that supports their well-being.
Smt. Patel urged AIIMS New Delhi to continuously examine areas where improvements can be made. Looking ahead, Smt. Patel called upon AIIMS New Delhi “to play an even more commanding role in advanced clinical care, nurture the next generation of compassionate healthcare professionals, undertake research addressing India’s unique health challenges and guide the broader AIIMS network as a unified family of institutions.” She emphasised that the quality of care and expertise developed at AIIMS New Delhi should have a wider national impact.
Smt. Patel expressed appreciation for the entire AIIMS family, including doctors, nurses, researchers, students, technicians, pharmacists, administrators, sanitation workers and security personnel, and acknowledged their collective contribution to the institution’s achievements. She called for patient care to become more accessible, safer and increasingly patient-centred, while emphasising that technology should strengthen and not replace the human relationship at the core of healing.
In her concluding remarks, Smt. Patel stated that AIIMS New Delhi has a distinguished past and a strong present, but carries an even greater responsibility to shape the future of Indian healthcare. She called for the institution to continue serving as a beacon of excellence, trust, affordability, innovation and selfless service to the people of India.
Smt. Patel also distributed awards to outstanding performers in different fields during the event.
As part of the celebrations, Smt. Anupriya Patel also inaugurated the exhibition
“AIIMS: Seven Decades of Healthcare Innovation”.
The exhibition showcases the journey of AIIMS and its contributions to healthcare and medical innovation through 95 posters, highlighting important milestones, achievements, initiatives and developments across the institution.
The exhibition also focuses on health education and community outreach. More than 1,500 school students will visit the exhibition and engage with interactive displays and live demonstrations on BMI assessment, healthy lifestyle and nutrition, blood sugar testing, common eye problems, dental and oral hygiene, organ donation and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) to learn how to revive critically ill patients. The exhibition will remain open from 25th to 27th September 2026.
Addressing the gathering, Director, AIIMS New Delhi, Dr. (Prof.) Nikhil Tandon highlighted the institution’s extraordinary scale of patient care, noting that AIIMS New Delhi recorded more than 50 lakh outpatient visits, admitted over 3.5 lakh patients and conducted nearly 3 lakh surgeries during the past year. He emphasized that these figures reflected the immense trust placed by people across the country in the institution. He also highlighted major advances in clinical care, including the milestone of more than 1,000 robotic surgeries and the successful performance of India’s first reported robot-assisted kidney transplant in a public sector institution. AIIMS also doubled its dialysis capacity and undertook over 300 highly complex super-microsurgical procedures.
Dr. Tandon further highlighted AIIMS New Delhi’s growing national role in capacity building, digital health, research and indigenous innovation. He noted that the institution welcomed around 1,000 new students and recruited over 300 faculty members during the year. He emphasised that AIIMS must extend its expertise beyond its campus through digital health, telemedicine and capacity-building initiatives to strengthen healthcare delivery across the country.
Dr. Shyam Sunder Kothari, Former Professor and Head, Department of Cardiology, AIIMS, New Delhi, faculty members, students and staff of AIIMS New Delhi were present on the occasion.
